zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 6; they obstruct the view downward from balconies and oceanview cabins on Decks 7–9, with Deck 7 experiencing the most pronounced blockage and Deck 9 the least.
zones.effect: You see the horizon and ocean clearly, but looking straight down reveals orange lifeboat roofs instead of water—the view feels elevated rather than intimate with the sea.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests who want that classic 'right on the water' feeling or enjoy watching the ship's wake directly below; irrelevant to those focused on horizon views, sunsets, or ports of call.

zones.what: Decks 10 and 11 directly above house the main pool deck (Aloha Pool, Waikiki Bar) with daytime activity, deck furniture dragging, and evening events.
zones.effect: Expect footfall noise, music, and occasional furniture movement overhead from late morning through evening; early sleepers may hear late-night pool deck stragglers.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and those turning in early should avoid; day-sleepers and those out enjoying the ship most of the time won't notice.

zones.what: The Aloha Café buffet sits directly above on Deck 11 mid and aft, operating from early morning through late evening with foot traffic, chair scraping, and service activity.
zones.effect: Overhead noise from breakfast prep starting around 6:00 AM, steady footfall during meal times, and occasional kitchen service sounds; quieter mid-afternoon and after dinner service ends.
zones.mattersTo: Early risers unbothered by morning buffet setup will find this irrelevant; late sleepers and those sensitive to intermittent daytime noise should steer clear.

zones.what: The Mardi Gras two-level show lounge occupies Decks 5 and 6 below, directly underneath mid and aft sections, with evening performances and occasional rehearsals.
zones.effect: Late-night shows (typically ending 10:00–11:00 PM) may transmit bass notes and applause; most guests report this as faint and infrequent, limited to show times.
zones.mattersTo: Sensitive sleepers who retire before 10:30 PM might notice; those out late or unbothered by muffled evening sound can ignore this.

zones.what: The Sky High Bar and observation area sit on Deck 13 and 14 forward, creating foot traffic and late-night socializing one or two decks above.
zones.effect: Late-evening and nighttime noise from bar patrons, conversation, and occasional live music drifts down; the forward observation deck sees steady use during scenic cruising.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers on Decks 11–12 forward should be cautious; heavy sleepers and those enjoying the bar themselves will find this a non-issue.

zones.what: Primary elevator and stair banks run through mid-ship on all main cabin decks, clustered around the main atrium and Grand Aloha Suite area.
zones.effect: Cabins very close to elevator lobbies experience door chimes, conversation, and foot traffic at all hours; those a few doors away gain convenience without meaningful noise.
zones.mattersTo: Mobility-limited guests and families with strollers benefit from proximity; noise-sensitive guests should choose cabins at least three doors away from elevator banks.

zones.what: Deck 4 aft sits low and near the engine room and propulsion machinery, transmitting low-frequency vibration and hum during maneuvering and open-ocean cruising.
zones.effect: A subtle, steady vibration underfoot and faint mechanical hum audible in quiet moments; most noticeable during port departures, arrivals, and speed changes.
zones.mattersTo: Vibration-sensitive sleepers and those bothered by low hum should avoid; budget-conscious guests unbothered by mechanical presence find excellent value here.

zones.what: Deck 4 forward sits near bow thrusters, which activate during docking and undocking with a pronounced rumble and vibration.
zones.effect: Noticeable vibration and mechanical noise during port arrivals and departures, typically lasting 10–20 minutes; silent during open-ocean cruising.
zones.mattersTo: Guests who sleep through port operations or enjoy watching docking maneuvers won't mind; light sleepers in port-intensive itineraries should choose higher or mid-ship.

zones.what: The anchor chain locker sits in the bow below forward cabins; anchor deployment creates a loud grinding and rattling sound, typically during early morning arrivals.
zones.effect: A brief (2–5 minute) but very loud metallic grinding wakes most sleepers when the anchor drops, usually between 6:00–8:00 AM on port days; silent at sea and in dock.
zones.mattersTo: Guests planning to sleep in on port mornings should avoid forward cabins entirely; early risers and those already awake for port arrivals won't be affected.

zones.what: Crew corridors (I-95) run through mid-ship with access points near the central elevator lobbies, creating occasional crew foot traffic through guest corridors during service hours.
zones.effect: Brief, infrequent crew movement through guest hallways during cabin service, meal delivery, and turndown; professional and quiet but noticeable to those near access doors.
zones.mattersTo: Most guests never notice; only those extremely sensitive to hallway activity or in cabins directly adjacent to crew doors should consider this.
